sentences.text: The present Detailed Accident Report (DAR) for compensation relates to grievous injuries suffered by the claimant in a road accident that took place that took place on 03.10.2018 at about 10.45 pm Near Blood Bank, Sadar Bazar Road, New Delhi regarding which an FIR bearing No.233/2018, under Sections 279/337 IPC was registered at PS Delhi Cantt.

The offending vehicle involved in this case is a Honda Activa Scooty bearing registration No. DL-5SCF-1451, which at the time of accident was being driven by respondent No.1, owned by respondent No.2 and insured with respondent No. 3.
2.

Succinctly put, facts of the case as per DAR are that on the aforesaid date, time and place of accident, the claimant along with his father and mother were returning home on a motorcycle bearing registration No. DL-3SCJ-7496 from Uttam Nagar via Sadar Bazar Road, Delhi and when they reached near Blood Bank, Sadar Bazar Road, one offending vehicle bearing registration No.
DL-8SCF-1451 being being driven by respondent No. 1 in a rash and negligent manner from front side hit against their motorcycle.
Due to said forceful hit, they fell on the road and sustained grievous injuries on all parts of their body.
They were removed to DDU Hospital, New Delhi, where doctor prepared their MLCs.

3. Joint reply has been filed on behalf of respondents No.1 & 2 stating that on the alleged date and time, respondent No.1/driver was driving the offending vehicle carefully and in a very slow speed and all of a sudden, one two wheeler came from wrong side and hit against his vehicle and due to said collusion, passengers of said two wheeler and respondent No. 1 fell down on the road and got injuries and were removed to hospital.
It is further stated that after sometime, respondent No. 1 came to know that an FIR has been registered against him.
It is further stated that respondent No.1 was holding a valid driving license at the time of alleged accident.
It is further stated that the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent No. 3 at the time of alleged accident.

4. Written Statement has also been filed on behalf of respondent No. 3/Insurance Company stating that the drivers of both the victim and offending vehicle were driving the vehicles under influence of Alcohol and were tested "Positive for Alcohol".

It is further stated that there was head collision which makes it evident that vehicles were driving on the same road but on opposite direction, hence insurer of second vehicle be also made party to the present DAR, however, no such application for impleading them has ever been filed on record by respondent No. 3.
5.

On 26.04.2017, the following consolidated issues were framed by the Ld. Predecessor of this Court as:-
1.

Whether Sh. Sunil Gosai (decesaed in D-83/19) sustained fatal injuries, Abeer Singh Gosai (injured in D- 84/19) and Smt. Rakhi Rawat Gosai (injured in D- 87/2019) sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 03.10.2018 at about 10.45 pm Near Blood Bank, Sadar Bazar Road, Delhi Cantt., New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL-8SCF-1451 being driven by respondent Abeer Singh Gasai vs Rahul Viktor on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38447831/

6. Heard arguments advanced by Sh. Dalip Singh, Ld. Counsel for the claimants and Sh. Sanjeev Srivastava, Ld. Counsel for respondent No. 3/Insurance Company.
However, none has appeared on behalf of R-1 and R-2 for tendering their final arguments.
The case record has also been perused.
The finding on the aforesaid issues is reproduced in succeeding paragraphs hereinafter.

1. Whether Sh. Sunil Gosai (decesaed in D-83/19) sustained fatal injuries, Abeer Singh Gosai (injured in D-84/19) and Smt. Rakhi Rawat Gosai (injured in D-87/2019) sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 03.10.2018 at about 10.45 pm Near Blood Bank, Sadar Bazar Road,
Delhi Cantt., New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL-8SCF-1451 being driven by respondent No. 1, owned by respondent No. 2 and insured with respondent No. 3? OPP.
7.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the claimant.

In order to prove the same, Smt. Rakhi Rawat Gosai, mother of claimant has examined herself as PW2, who tendered her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex. PW2/A wherein she has deposed that her husband was driving a motorcycle bearing registration No. DL- 3SCJ-7496 whereas she and her son were sitting as pillion riders and they were returning home from Uttam Nagar and when they reached near Blood Bank, Sadar Bazar Road, New Delhi, one vehicle bearing registration No. DL-8SCF-1451 being driven by respondent No. 1 in a rash and negligent manner came from front side and hit against their motorcycle.
They fell down on the road and thereafter, they all were removed to DDU hospital, where doctor prepared their MLCs.

8. During cross examination conducted on behalf of Insurance Company, the witness denied the suggestion that the accident took place due to contributory negligence of her deceased husband and not due to exclusive negligence of respondent No. 1. and also denied that her husband was drunk at the time of driving the bike.
Despite opportunity given, respondents No. 1 & 2 did not cross examine the said witness.

9. During the course of final arguments, Ld. Counsel for Insurance Company has argued that the deceased and respondent no.1 were driving their vehicles under the influence of alcohol at the relevant time of accident which is apparent from their MLCs filed along with the DAR.
Perusal of their MLCs reveal that the smell of alcohol is present.

However, the arguments advanced on behalf of Insurance Company do not find any force as the FSL report placed on record clearly mention that there is no traces of alcohol in the blood sample of deceased and no quantity of alcohol has been mentioned in the MLC of respondent no. 1.
10.

Further, Ld. Counsel for Insurance Company has argued that there was head on collision between the vehicles which is apparent from the site plan and hence, the contributory should be deducted from the awarded amount.

Per contra, Ld. Counsel for claimants has argued that the offending vehicle came from the wrong side and there is no question of contributory negligence on Abeer Singh Gasai vs Rahul Viktor on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38447831/

11. It may also be noted that even the Investigating Officer has concluded that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing No. DL-8SCF-1451.
The site plan does not show that any of the vehicle was coming from wrong side and hence, the question of contributory negligence does not arise in the present matter.
Moreover, it has not been disputed that respondent no. 1 has been charge-sheeted in the aforesaid FIR for offences punishable under Sections 279/338/304A IPC.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.,
2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently.

sentences.text: It has been further observed that even when the accused were to be acquitted in the criminal case, the same may be of no effect on the assessment of the liability required in respect of motor accident cases by the Tribunal.
12. Pertinently, respondent no. 1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to rebut his involvement in the aforesaid accident, which he has failed to do.

Therefore,
an adverse inference is drawn against the respondent no. 1/driver in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.

sentences.text: It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants

sentences.text: were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.

14. In view of foregoing discussion, it stands proved on preponderance of probability that the aforesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-8-SCF-1451 and the said vehicle at that time was being driven by respondent No.
1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3.
Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the claimants and against the respondents.
Whether the claimant is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

15 . As the issue No.1 has been proved in favour of the claimant, he has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered by him in the accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
16. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which Abeer Singh Gasai vs Rahul Viktor on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38447831/
4 compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.

17.

Having considered the ratio of aforesaid judgment, the compensation payable to claimant is assessed hereinafter under the following heads as:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 18.
PW2 has tendered on record copy of discharge summary of her son as Ex. PW2/7 (colly) as per which the claimant was referred from DDU Hospital for NCCT head and neuro opinion to Safdarjung Hospital.
It further reflects that the claimant is a case of pain in right arm and advised X-ray for fracture right humerus.

19. PW2 in her affidavit has not tendered on record medical bills of her son, however, there are certain medical bills on record which seems to have not been reimbursed as the originals have been placed on record and hence, these medical bills are taken into consideration which are totalling to a sum of Rs. 5,355/-.
20.
Needless to say, the insurance company has not led any evidence to show that the said bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the claimant in the aforesaid accident.
In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve that she has spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses of her son.
Hence, the claimant is held entitled to Rs. 5,355/- towards his medical expenses.
(ii) Mental and Physical Shock, Pain and Sufferings & Loss of Amenities.

sentences.text: As stated above, the claimant had suffered grievous injuries in the accident.

Though, it is not possible to exactly compensate him for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which he had actually suffered because of the above injuries, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/-
each is being awarded to him towards mental and physical shock & for pain and sufferings.

Further,
an amount of Rs.25,000/- is also awarded to him towards the loss of amenities suffered by him during the said period of his treatment.
Thus, he is awarded total amount of Rs.1,25,000/- under this head.
(iii) Conveyance, Special Diet and Attendant Charges 22.
PW2 in her affidavit Ex. PW2/A is silent with regard to the amounts spent towards special diet and conveyance in respect of her son.

Still this Tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of conveyance for claimant for frequently visiting the hospital and doctors in connection with his treatment and special diet for his early recovery from the injuries suffered because of the accident.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, an amount of Rs.20,000/- is being awarded to the claimant towards special diet and Rs. 10,000/- towards conveyance.

23. Keeping in view the nature of injuries, the claimant would have required assistance of some family member/attendant for doing his daily routine work for atleast six months, therefore, a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month for six months is also being awarded to the claimant towards attendant charges.

The injured/claimant is thus entitled to an amount of Rs.90,000/- (Rs.10,000/- + Rs.
20,000 + Rs. 10,000/- per month X 6 months) under this head.
(iv) Loss of education 24.

Though there is no specific evidence on record to show as to how long and to what extent the studies of claimant were affected due to the above injuries, but keeping in view the duration of his treatment and nature of the injuries, this tribunal can take note of the same and hence, a lump-sum amount of Rs.25,000/- is also being awarded to the claimant under this head.
(v) Loss of childhood 25.

The claimant was aged around 6 years at the relevant time of accident and this is the age of claimant to enjoy childhood and play with their friends which he had lost for some duration due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Hence, considering the age of claimant as well as nature of injuries, a lumpsum amount of Rs. 25,000/- is also being awarded to the claimant under this head.

In view of finding on issue number 2, the claimant is held entitled to a sum of Rs.2,70,355/-

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The site plan does not show that any of the vehicle was coming from wrong side and hence, the question of contributory negligence does not arise in the present matter.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.,
2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently.
Therefore,
an adverse inference is drawn against the respondent no. 1/driver in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
13.
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.
were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
16. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.
Needless to say, the insurance company has not led any evidence to show that the said bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the claimant in the aforesaid accident.
In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve that she has spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses of her son.
Hence, the claimant is held entitled to Rs. 5,355/- towards his medical expenses.

each is being awarded to him towards mental and physical shock & for pain and sufferings.

an amount of Rs.25,000/- is also awarded to him towards the loss of amenities suffered by him during the said period of his treatment.

The claimant was aged around 6 years at the relevant time of accident and this is the age of claimant to enjoy childhood and play with their friends which he had lost for some duration due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
